intro: Editing is the slowest part of posting. Claude Code can do most of it from plain-English instructions: it writes the code that renders captions, zooms and overlays onto your clip, then you watch and ask for changes.

free.title: Step 1: Set up Claude Code
free.body: If you haven't yet, install Claude Code in VS Code (see my Claude Code Starter Setup guide). Make a folder called "reels" and put one raw clip in it.

free.title: Step 2: Start the video project
free.body: Copy this inIn this folder, set up a video project using Remotion (or another code-based video tool you recommend) that renders vertical 1080x1920 videos from my clip [file name]. Install only what's needed, explain each step in plain English, and render a 5-second test.

free.title: Step 3: Captions and zooms
free.body: Copy this inTranscribe my clip and add word-by-word captions, 2-4 words at a time, bold white with a dark outline, centered in the lower third. Add a quick punch-in zoom on these words: [3-5 key words]. Render it.

free.title: Step 4: Overlays and title cards
free.body: Copy this inAdd: a title card for the first 2 seconds saying [hook]; the screenshot [file] sliding in over the top half when I say [phrase]; and an end card with my call to action [CTA]. Keep my face visible.

free.title: Step 5: Save your effects library
free.body:
Copy this inTurn each effect we made into a reusable component with a clear name (captions, punch-zoom, slide-in screenshot, title card, end card) and write a one-line README for each so I can say "add a punch-zoom on X" next time.

Use only clips, music and images you have the rights to.
